logical report of past performance) and 'probability' (an inductive prediction). It posits that choosing the best-corroborated theory is not an inference that the theory will hold, but a methodological rule to minimize the risk of acting on a theory already known to be false. The mechanism relies on the concept of 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) to argue that while we cannot know a theory is true, a highly corroborated theory has withstood attempts to show it is less like the truth than its rivals.
